newsitem.title: UK: Anti-handgun lobby demands complete British ban.
newsitem.headline: Anti-handgun lobby demands complete British ban.

text.p: British campaigners against firearms warned the government on Sunday they would not accept a partial ban on handguns in the aftermath of the Dunblane massacre.

The warning came ahead of publication this week of the report of a judicial inquiry into the tragedy in which unhinged gunman Thomas Hamilton killed 16 children and a teacher at a primary school in the Scottish town.

But Ann Pearston, who has helped to organise the Dunblane Snowdrop Petition on handguns, said campaigners might put up a candidate against Scottish Secretary Michael Forsyth at the forthcoming general election unless he went for a complete ban on handguns.

The Sunday Times newspaper reported that the government, under pressure from an active gun lobby, was planning a milder reform of the law, forcing handgun owners to keep them under lock and key at registered gun clubs.

Forsyth is widely tipped to lose his Stirling seat at the general election which Major must call by next May. At the last election in 1992, he had a majority of just 703 votes over the opposition Labour Party.
Hamilton held licences for the four semi-automatic handguns he used in Britain's worst gun massacre in March, even though he was widely regarded as a social misfit.
Opinion polls show 70 percent of Britons want a handgun ban, but the influential gun lobby says this would be an infringement of liberties and would not prevent gun crimes.
The Sunday Times said that only if Cullen unambiguously recommended a total ban on handguns would the government comply.

Other British newspapers reported that lawyers acting for parents of the children killed at Dunblane would consider whether to sue the police for negligence in not monitoring Hamilton more closely after reading Cullen's report.
